traits.note: FNA vol. 28, Homalothecium (Ignatov; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants in loose to dense tufts or mats, green to rich golden; stems creeping, pinnate; stem leaves erect-appressed when dry, lanceolate, strongly plicate; seta red-brown; capsule inclined to erect, red-brown, cylindric. Typical values are H. sericeum, the silky wall moss (same volume): light green to golden or brownish yellow; stems to 5 cm, branches 5-7 mm, curved and secund from the surface; stem leaves 1.8-2.4 x 0.6-0.8 mm, branch leaves 1-2 x 0.2-0.5 mm, appressed dry, spreading moist; seta 1-2 cm; capsule erect, cylindric, 2-3 mm; on rock and rock faces.

traits.leaf_shape.note: FNA vol. 28, Homalothecium sericeum (efloras, read 2026-11-05): stem leaves triangular-lanceolate; branch leaves narrowly lanceolate.

traits.substrates.note: FNA gives rock and rock faces for North America, where it is rare; in Europe H. sericeum is one of the commonest mosses of old walls, limestone and the bark of trees (general bryological knowledge; to cite from Atherton et al., Mosses and Liverworts of Britain and Ireland, 2010).

traits.substrate_reaction.note: Base-rich rock, mortar and limestone, as in European floras; see the note on substrates.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: Estimate as for other pleurocarp mats; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.

traits.capsule_shape.note: FNA vol. 28, Homalothecium sericeum: capsule cylindric, straight or slightly curved. (efloras, read 2026-11-05)

traits.operculum_form.note: FNA vol. 28, Homalothecium: operculum long-conic and gradually rostrate, sometimes conic; H. sericeum long-conic, short-rostrate. (efloras, read 2026-11-05)

traits.dry_branch_posture.note: BBS species finder, Homalothecium sericeum (read 2026-11-05, as summarised in a search): when dry, the distinctive curled-up look of the crowded secondary branches makes this common species easy to identify; H. lutescens keeps straight branches when dry. NatureSpot: the side branches curve upwards and inwards when dry and straighten again on wetting. FNA vol. 28: branches curved and secund from the surface.

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, about 20 a taxon, script moss_colour.py): the median linear r/g and b/g of the moss pixels (Homalothecium r/g 0.94, b/g 0.27). Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible (Lovelock and Robinson 2002, Plant Cell Environ. 25: 1239, Antarctic Grimmia; moss biocrust albedo about 0.11 against 0.20 for bare soil, Sci. Total Environ. 2020), the canopy's own shade darkening the shell further.

traits.spore_diameter_m.note: FNA vol. 28, Homalothecium (Ignatov; efloras, read 2026-11-05): spores 10-21 µm.
